chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

When the slaughtered animal is cut open and there is a fetus in its womb, he said: 'If it is fully formed, eat it, for its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother. And if it is not fully formed, do not eat it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating a fetus found inside a slaughtered animal according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a fully formed fetus inherits the ritual slaughter status of its mother, rendering it permissible to consume without a separate slaughter, while an immature fetus is excluded. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'inheritance of ruling' (tarkhib al-hukm) in cases of biological dependency, distinguishing between complete and incomplete development. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the conditions of meat purity in classical fiqh.
